patients.label: 60-year-old woman with sudden right-eye visual disturbance after a sneezing fit, diagnosed with Valsalva retinopathy

identity_evidence.quote: A 60-year-old female with a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented to the ED due to vision changes in the right eye.

attribution_limitations: Who made the diagnosis and when is not consistent: the abstract says ophthalmology diagnosed Valsalva retinopathy during the ED consultation, while the Case report says the diagnosis was made after the repeat ultrasound at retina clinic the next morning.
The sneezing fit is described by the discussion as the likely cause of the pre-retinal hemorrhage; this is a hedged cause and is not recorded as an asserted cause.
The date or interval of the vitrectomy after the diagnosis is not stated; "eventually" is the only time wording.

The discussion states vitreous opacities and a fully attached retina for this patient but does not say which examination (ED point-of-care ultrasound, ophthalmology exam or next-morning repeat ultrasound) or time they refer to.
